intro: Meer Dividbrook claims the analysis is handled by AI models, so newcomers can follow signals instead of charts. The claim is easy to publish. The verification is what this review looks for.
The desk combines AI signals with manual control. Newcomers can start on the practice account, fund US$250 when ready, and trade 9 assets through the partner broker.
The scorecard reflects what the platform publishes, not what its ads promise. We checked the claims against the pages, looked for independent verification, and marked the gaps we found.
whatItClaims: Bonds are the headline market, alongside crypto and other assets.
Machine-generated signals combined with rule-based models.
Risk settings adjustable without switching account type.
Identity verification completed before live trading.
Entry from $250, free demo, no platform fee and 24-hour withdrawals.
whatWeChecked: The bond-first pitch: fixed income as the core, crypto as the volatile sleeve.
The bond coverage: asserted in marketing, hard to confirm in the demo.
The asset balance: more coins than bonds in the actual lineup.
The operator gap: company, regulator, licence and broker all unnamed.
The fee framing: no platform fee, broker spread on every trade.
The performance record: returns advertised without independent audit.
